newsitem.title: UK: Eurpean charter airlines face growth problems.
newsitem.headline: Eurpean charter airlines face growth problems.

text.p: Charter airline growth potential is being impeded by inadequate airport facilities, air traffic control delays and poor ground handling standards despite carrying over 50 percent of intra-European air traffic, said Marcel Pisters, director general of the International Air Carrier Association (IACA).
He told an IATA conference that moves by the European Commission to liberalise ground handling facilities that were "very disappointing".
A proposed directive was being watered down by "so many possible exemptions," he explained, that it did nothing for non-scheduled airlines. IACA represents 41 European charter carriers.
There was too much emphasis on major gateways and a lack of investment and planning at many of Europe's tourist-receiving airports.

Other moves by Brussels to alleviate airport congestion through the introduction of a so-called "monetised secondary trading" system encouraging the buying and selling of arrival and departure slots by airlines was another sources of concern, he said.
It would impede market entry and place cash-rich scheduled airlines in a dominant position at important charter hubs.

European plans to end duty-free privileges on airline sales in June 1999 was another blow to operators dedicated to providing low-cost services to the leisure segment of the air transport market and would be resisted.
"As non-scheduled airlines," said Pisters, "we rely on such inflight sales to a greater extent than scheduled airlines and our profitability will be affected to a much greater degree."

The charter airline body was also vigorously opposing state handouts to national flag carriers: "We have to compete on a playing field that is less than level," he said, "when you take into account the vast sums of cash being injected into these airlines with the blessing of the European Commission.
"Our association continues to pressure governments and the Commission to outlaw such capital injections," he added. - Air Cargo Newsroom Tel+44 171 542 7706 Fax+44 171 542 5017
